desc: One object turned through a full 360 as a rendered video. The deliverable is the video, not an asset.
source_prompt: a single ceramic teapot standing upright, curved spout, round lid with a knob, one loop handle, the whole teapot inside the frame with margin on all sides, three-quarter view, flat mid-grey seamless background, even frontal light, no cast shadow, no table, no cups, no steam
output: 90-frame 1024x1024 orbit MP4 (3.6 s at 25 fps) plus a .spz Gaussian splat file (~3.2 MB). No GLB mesh - see note.
usable_for: showing a 3D result to a person, client or art-direction review, concept sign-off, reference turntable for a modeller
not_usable_for: any mesh use whatsoever - a splat has no faces, no edges, no UVs. It cannot be imported into a game engine, decimated, retopologised or 3D printed.
note: Correction worth knowing: this graph's SaveGLB node is fed by SplatToFile3D with format spz, and the file it actually wrote on this box is triposplat_splat_00001_.spz, not a .glb. Despite the node name there is no mesh on this path at all. The .spz opens in Gaussian-splat viewers, not in Blender. BiRefNet mattes the subject inside this graph before reconstruction, so the background is removed for you - but a busy or low-contrast background still defeats the matte and leaves floating gaussians orbiting the subject, so keep the plain background anyway.
